mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for ≥3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.0%, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher short-term rates, which compresses the real discount rate and depresses S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the mean of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05), or ΔCPIAUCSL ≤ +1.5% for the next 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 20,000 suggests labor market slack, lowering growth expectations and reducing S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥20,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly below the mean of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05), or monthly PAYEMS growth < 10,000 for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) falls by more than 5% in a month relative to the prior month, it signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or HOUST declines by ≤4% for the next 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) index below 105 indicates supply-side weakness, lowering aggregate demand expectations and generating negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not persistently negative across 3 consecutive months with INDPRO < 105 (median), or INDPRO recovers above 106 within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% and 3% respectively in a month indicate dual demand and supply pressures, producing a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% AND RSAFS decreases by ≥3% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative when both proxies show recovery (GDPC1 up ≥2%, RSAFS up ≥3%) within the next month, or the interaction IC > 0.05 over a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for 2 consecutive months is interpreted as a labor market tightening, raising policy rate expectations and depressing S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases for 2 consecutive months and remains below 4.5%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or UNRATE recovers above 4.5% within 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling UNRATE (<4.0%) and rising FEDFUNDS (>4.75%) over 3 consecutive months, the combination signals persistent monetary tightening that compresses equity discounting, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for 3 months AND FEDFUNDS > 4.75% for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05), or either proxy breaks the trigger condition for the next 2 months.
